claude_code.how: The README documents `claude mcp add -s user jcodemunch -- uvx jcodemunch-mcp`, or a preinstalled jcodemunch-mcp executable. Its init path also installs prompt policy and offers enforcement hooks and project indexing; the manual instructions ask the agent to call jcodemunch_guide. This is a broader default than merely making an optional project server available.

codex.how: CLIENTS.md recommends a preinstalled executable, resolved to an absolute path in [mcp_servers.jcodemunch], with no arguments. Its example uses $HOME/.codex/config.toml; init refuses a uvx fallback for Codex because first-run installer output can corrupt the initial JSON-RPC exchange.

official_baseline_claims.claim: Upstream benchmarks search_symbols followed by focused get_symbol_source retrieval against both grep-and-read and read-all baselines on pinned public repositories. Its advertised savings are specific to those retrieval workloads and are not a measurement of this adaptation.

The current server still supplies MCP initialization instructions directing clients to prefer jCodeMunch over Read/Grep/Glob/Bash for code navigation, for both Counter and full surfaces. The server inserts _mcp_instructions into the initialization response, so this is client-facing server policy rather than only README advice.

limitations.text: Upstream says targeted function, method and class edits benefit most; work that genuinely needs an entire file has no corresponding source-selection advantage.

For Codex, executable availability and a clean stdout handshake matter; configuring an on-demand package runner is not equivalent to a qualified installed-binary integration. The client guide also identifies noninteractive elicitation declines as a distinct client-side failure mode.

The base package reports an anonymous aggregate savings counter by default; upstream provides a share_savings opt-out. Such counters and marketing totals are separate from task-level exact artifact comparisons.

native_adaptation.how_we_install: Reviewed the checkout matching origin/main@34c56340e636ad3d3daeb8482d48d1d8f0b135ae. manifests/stack.json:1672 identifies the supporting component and source commit 8f7b34abe16fb459e0bf1c04747d584216dfe32e. Install the pinned package with `uv tool install --python 3.13 jcodemunch-mcp==1.108.319` in the owned uv-tool prefix, exposing ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/jcodemunch-mcp (adoption/bootstrap.md:286; recipes/README.md:434). This is an explicit bootstrap step; jCodeMunch is not selected by the automated adoption profiles or listed in either platform pins file (adoption/manifest.json; adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json; adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json).
native_adaptation.claude_wiring: Project opt-in uses `claude mcp add --scope local jcodemunch` with the installed executable, or a project .mcp.json entry; CODE_INDEX_PATH points to $HOME/.code-index and JCODEMUNCH_SHARE_SAVINGS=0 (adoption/bootstrap.md:334). adoption/mcp/claude-user.json deliberately omits jcodemunch, and adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json does not register it. The shipped evidence-reviewer and isolated-builder explicitly grant mcp__jcodemunch__route and mcp__jcodemunch__order, usable where the project registers the server (examples/claude-native/agents/evidence-reviewer.md:4; examples/claude-native/agents/isolated-builder.md:4).
native_adaptation.codex_wiring: adoption/templates/project.codex.config.template.toml:25 deliberately keeps [mcp_servers.jcodemunch] at project scope with the installed ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/jcodemunch-mcp executable and startup_timeout_sec=60; the user template has no jcodemunch entry. Live `codex mcp list --json` plus `codex mcp get jcodemunch --json` confirm the main checkout's server, while the same merged list in a neutral directory lacks it. The untracked host-only .codex/config.toml:33 is therefore a real local registration for this checkout, not proof of user-scope or fresh-worktree availability.
native_adaptation.lane_rule: Explicitly index selected code, search, then retrieve a returned symbol ID; check original source and freshness. Use the Counter surface and keep sharing, AI/paid summaries, watchers, cross-repository defaults and external context providers disabled for this recipe (recipes/README.md:432; docs/token-session-handbook.md:108; docs/token-session-handbook.md:131).

deviations_from_upstream.what: Project scope in both clients is an intentional departure from upstream's user-scope examples. Current main still records this decision in docs/decisions/2026-09-23-claude-user-profile.md:127 and docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md:83. Upstream still injects the tool-preference instruction that motivated it (https://github.com/jgravelle/jcodemunch-mcp/blob/ffe99fdee833435442a5ff506259f68cae872c39/src/jcodemunch_mcp/server.py#L359-L400).
deviations_from_upstream.why: Those decisions retain the historical transcript and sealed-retrieval evidence, including the corpus's Markdown coverage gap, and conclude that a globally loaded preference conflicts with this catalog's rg/Serena/SocratiCode routing. They do not retire jCodeMunch or claim that the historical comparison applies to every workload. Fresh worktrees consequently need their own registration, consistent with the assembled card's scope shortfall.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Preserve the intentional scope; render the project entry into each opted-in worktree and verify it there. Reconsider user scope only under the decision's Codex-specific retrieval-evidence overturn condition.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The focused recipe still prints `codex mcp add jcodemunch` before explaining that the tested adoption used project configuration, whereas the current scope decision and project template require explicit per-project registration (recipes/README.md:441; recipes/README.md:449; adoption/templates/project.codex.config.template.toml:25).
deviations_from_upstream.why: The recipe distinguishes the CLI configuration from the tested project entry, but its copyable command can lead a new adopter to bypass the deliberate project-scope policy.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Make the recipe's Codex example render the project template and verify registration from the intended worktree; explain any user-scope CLI example as a different choice.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The adaptation uses a preinstalled pinned binary and selected-code workflow instead of upstream init's broader prompt/hook installation, and opts out of savings sharing and optional enrichment (recipes/README.md:434; recipes/README.md:452; https://github.com/jgravelle/jcodemunch-mcp/blob/ffe99fdee833435442a5ff506259f68cae872c39/README.md#recommended-one-command).
deviations_from_upstream.why: This preserves the catalog's existing retrieval lanes and bounded indexing. The installed executable also matches upstream's specific Codex handshake recommendation; optional watcher and enrichment behavior cannot be credited as enabled here.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Keep explicit opt-in and freshness checks, and measure any future hook or enrichment adoption separately. Do not infer client use or exact token savings from the upstream counter alone.

The newer source-verified comparison is 25,440→570 o200k_base tokens (97.8%), eligible for MCPorter-rendered search_symbols plus get_symbol_source against a whole-file baseline, with the one-time index response excluded and native-client rendering unmeasured (../rr/jcodemunch-mcp/records.json#jcodemunch-mcp-74-compare-retrieval). The historical native Claude result is separately 22,043→443 (98.0%), while the newer +27,267 native ledger delta is an estimate rather than the exact 24,870-token artifact reduction; no successful fresh-worktree Codex comparison is available (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json; ../rr/jcodemunch-mcp/records.json#jcodemunch-mcp-14-counter-after).
